item.title: Bohr inequalities and Landau-type estimates for harmonic Poisson extensions of $L^p$ boundary functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.33171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes sharp quantitative bounds governing the Bohr phenomenon, Landau-type distortion, and geometric univalence for complex-valued harmonic mappings on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ parameterized by boundary data in the Lebesgue spaces $L^{p}(\mathbb{T})$ for $1 \le p \le \infty$, where $\mathbb{T} = \partial\mathbb{D}$. First, we resolve the classical coefficient problem for bounded harmonic mappings by incorporating an integral Parseval constraint rather than crude individual bounds, establishing the sharp Bohr radius as $r_H(a) = \sqrt{(1-a)/(3+a)}$ for a fixed initial term $\vert{}a_0\vert{} = aM$. Second, this framework is extended to the $L^p$ setting under the vanishing normalization $f(0)=0$, explicitly characterizing the sharp Bohr radius as $r_{p} = (2C_{q}+1)^{-1}$, where the structural constant $C_{q}$ is intrinsically linked to the conjugate exponent $q$. Finally, under standard normalization, we determine explicit formulations for both the radius of univalence $r_{0}$ and the corresponding radius of the inscribed Schlicht disk $R_{0}$. The sharpness of all analytical constants and radii is verified through the construction of concrete extremal configurations derived from the Poisson kernel.
item.dc:creator: Molla Basir Ahamed, Vasudevarao Allu, Rajesh Hossain

item.title: Cohomology growth for pseudoeffective line bundles on compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.33601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $L$ be a pseudoeffective line bundle with a singular metric $h$ satisfying $\Theta_h(L)\geq0$ on a compact K\"ahler manifold $X$ of dimension $n$. Let $\mathcal{I}(h^k)$ denote the multiplier ideal sheaf of $h^k$. For every holomorphic vector bundle $E$ and $0\le q\le n$, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim}_{\mathbb{C}}H^q\!\left(X,E\otimes L^k\otimes\mathcal{I}(h^k)\right)=O(k^{n-q}),$$ which gives an affirmative answer to Matsumura's growth problem. As an application, we resolve the cohomology growth problem for nef line bundles raised by Demailly.
item.dc:creator: Hongrong Chen, Guokuan Shao, Wenxuan Wang, Xiangyu Zhou

item.title: The finiteness of $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.33696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, motivated by J.-P. Demailly's finiteness argument, we establish a criterion for a closed linear operator between Hilbert spaces to have closed range of finite codimension. We then apply this criterion to give affirmative answers to two questions of T. Ohsawa on the finiteness of $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups in a unified manner. To this end, we adapt Demailly's compactness argument to a family of complete approximating metrics, thereby establishing the finite dimensionality of the $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups with respect to a possibly incomplete metric. Furthermore, we extend the answers to the setting of singular metrics with quasi-plurisubharmonic local weights.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen, Yi Li

item.title: Singularities in global pluripotential theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.33697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This book is an expanded version of the author's lecture notes at the Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (IASM) at Zhejiang University. We systematically develop the theory of plurisubharmonic singularities on compact K\"ahler manifolds and relate it to the non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and toric pluripotential theory.
item.dc:creator: Mingchen Xia

item.title: An answer to "Hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundaries" by X. Wang and C. Yang
item.description: arXiv:2611.33755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a variant of the recent proof concerning hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundary.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Harz

item.title: A Characterization of Douglas Weights
item.description: arXiv:2611.34221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A weight $\omega$ on the unit disc is a \emph{Douglas weight} if the $\omega$-energy of the Poisson extension of every Lipschitz function $f$ on the unit circle equals $\iint|f(\zeta)-f(\lambda)|^2\,d\J_\omega$ for some positive symmetric measure $\J_\omega$ off the diagonal. For radial weights, we show that this holds if and only if \[ j_\omega(\theta) = \int_0^1 \frac{\omega(r)}{r}\, \partial_\theta^2 P(r^2,\theta)\,dr \geq 0, \qquad 0<\theta\leq\pi, \] where $P(x,\theta)$ denotes the Poisson kernel. We also obtain a complete characterization of the Douglas weights among arbitrary weights. The class of Douglas weights strictly contains the nonnegative superharmonic weights, and we give examples that are neither superharmonic nor subharmonic.
item.dc:creator: Youssef Elmadani, Abdelouahab Hanine

item.title: On the Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.34239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The notion of partial-slice monogenic functions has recently been introduced to provide a unified framework encompassing both monogenic and slice monogenic functions over Clifford algebras. In this new setting, we establish some fractional Laplacian identities for the Cauchy kernels and their derivatives in the sense of tempered distributions. These identities allow us to prove a termwise Fueter--Sce--Qian theorem for partial-slice monogenic functions represented by convergent Laurent series consisting only of principal parts.
item.dc:creator: Qinghai Huo, Irene Sabadini, Zhenghua Xu

item.title: Infinite Hyper-Order of Entire Solutions of a First-Order Differential Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.34469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\varphi$ be a transcendental entire function of finite order. We prove that every entire solution of $$g'=e^\varphi g+1$$ has infinite hyper-order. Then we prove the Br\"uck's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: D. H. Zhao, J, Zhang, S. S. Yang, L. W. Liao

item.title: Entire function related to shift and difference operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.34660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the uniqueness problems of entire functions involving difference operators. First, we examine the case where $f-a$, $\Delta_c^n f-b$, and $\Delta_c^{n+2}f-b$ share $0$ CM (counting multiplicities), where $a$ and $b$ are two entire small functions of $f$ such that $\Delta_c^m a \equiv 0$ ($1 \le m \le n$), and $b$ is $c$-periodic. As a consequence, we establish two main results, one of which resolves a conjecture posed by Farissi et al. \cite{FLBA1}. Second, we obtain a uniqueness theorem for an entire function $f(z)$ when $f(z)$, $f(z+c)$, and $\Delta_c f(z)$ share a single value, thereby improving and generalizing the corresponding result of Farissi et al. \cite{FLA1} by removing the growth restriction on the order of $f$. Third, we establish uniqueness results for $f(z)$ when $f(z)$ and $\Delta_c^k f(z)$ share a value, which improve and generalize the findings of Chen et al. \cite{CCL2} and Huang and Zhang \cite{HZ1}. Finally, we provide several examples to demonstrate that our results are best possible in certain senses.
item.dc:creator: Sujoy Majumder, Lata Mahato, Ashoke Das

item.title: Norm of the Generalized Hilbert Matrix Operator Between Some Spaces of Analytic Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.33616v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the generalized Hilbert operator \[ \mathcal H_bf(z)=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^b}{(1-tz)^{b+1}}f(t)\,dt, \qquad b>0, \] on several spaces of analytic functions in the unit disk. For logarithmically weighted Korenblum spaces, we obtain an exact supremum representation and a lower estimate for the norm of the mapping from $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$ to $H_\alpha^\infty$. We then establish two-sided estimates and characterize the boundedness range of $\mathcal H_b$ on the $\alpha$-Bloch spaces $\mathcal B^\alpha$. We also derive norm bounds for the mapping from $H^\infty$ into the endpoint Zygmund-type space $\Lambda_1^{1,*}$. Furthermore, we give a norm representation for $\mathcal H_b:H_\alpha^\infty\to\mathcal B^{\alpha+1}$ and identify a norm-attaining function. In particular, for $0<\alpha\leq2/3$, the norm is expressed explicitly in terms of a Beta function. Finally, we obtain an exact supremum representation of the norm of $\mathcal H_b$ on $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$, together with explicit norm estimates. Our results extend those of Hao et al. [J. Geom. Anal. 35 (2025), Paper No. 184] for the classical Hilbert matrix operator ($b=0$) to the generalized case $b>0$.
item.dc:creator: Shaoyang Feng, Shanli Ye

item.title: Independence of Thurston eigenvalues and Lyapunov exponents for quadratic rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.34186v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study post-critically finite quadratic rational maps $f: \mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$ where the two critical points lie in the same cycle. The Thurston eigenvalues of $f$ are those of the derivative of the Thurston pullback map $\sigma_f$ at its fixed point. Addressing questions of Buff--Epstein--Koch, we construct a sequence of real, bitransitive centres in the critical orbit relation curve $C_2$ which degenerates in moduli space, and whose Lyapunov exponents tend to infinity whilst the Thurston eigenvalues satisfy $\frac{1}{10}< |\lambda|<1$. We also show the Thurston eigenvalues across all bitransitive centres in $C_2$ have a spectral gap on compact subsets of the curve.
item.dc:creator: Ayesha Bennett, Holly Krieger

item.title: Connectedness Principle in the Complex Analytic Setting
item.description: arXiv:2611.34654v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that if $(X,B)$ is a normal compact K\"ahler pair and $f:X\to Z$ is a proper morphism with connected fibers to a normal compact K\"ahler variety $Z$ such that $(-K_X+B)$ is nef over $Z$, then $\mathrm{Nklt}(X,B)\cap f^{-1}(z)$ has at most two connected components for every $z\in Z$. More generally, we prove the result for generalized pairs whose nef part is allowed to be transcendental. Moreover, we record that the same result holds for projective morphism between analytic varieties (possibly non-compact).
item.dc:creator: Swapnajit Das

item.title: Cyclic polynomials in mixed-weighted Dirichlet-type spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.34661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)\in\mathbb R^3$, we investigate cyclic polynomials in the mixed-weighted Dirichlet-type space $\mathscr{D}_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}$ of holomorphic functions $f(z_1,z_2)=\sum_{m,n\geq0}a_{m,n}z_1^mz_2^n$ on the unit bidisk satisfying $$ \sum_{m,n\geq0}|a_{m,n}|^2 (m+1)^{\alpha_1}(n+1)^{\alpha_2} (m+n+1)^{\alpha_3}<\infty. $$ We give a complete characterization of cyclic polynomials in terms of their zero sets and the parameters $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3$. Our results extend previously known characterizations for anisotropic and total-degree Dirichlet-type spaces on the unit bidisk.
item.dc:creator: Rajkamal Nailwal, Aljaz Zalar

item.title: Borel exceptional values in several complex variables and their applications to shared values of shifts and difference operators
item.description: arXiv:2602.14619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate shared value problems for shifts and higher-order difference operators of meromorphic and entire functions in several complex variables. Using Nevanlinna theory in $\mathbb{C}^n$, we obtain new uniqueness theorems when functions share values counting or ignoring multiplicities, extending several classical one-variable results to higher dimensions. A key contribution of this work appears in Section 2, where we establish fundamental results on Borel exceptional values in several complex variables. These propositions provide the main tools for proving our principal theorems. As applications, we derive conditions ensuring that a transcendental entire function satisfies $\Delta_c^{k} \equiv d\hspace{.05cc} f$ and we study meromorphic solutions of certain partial differential-difference equations, obtaining growth estimates and structural descriptions of entire solutions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of such shared value problems for higher-order difference operators in several complex variables.
item.dc:creator: Abhijit Banerjee, Sujoy Majumder, Jhilik Banerjee

item.title: Teichm\"uller space of a closed set in the Riemann sphere
item.description: arXiv:2603.05328v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Teichm\"uller space of a closed set in the Riemann sphere is a simply connected complex Banach manifold. Its complex structure follows from Lieb isomorphism. In this paper, we show the conformal naturality of Lieb isomorphism. We then study Douady-Earle section for these Teichm\"uller spaces. In particular, we study the real-analyticity of Douady-Earle section for classical Teichm\"uller spaces. We give two explicit examples of maximal holomorphic motions over simply connected complex Banach manifolds. As an application of the real-analyticity of the Douady-Earle section for the classical Teichm\"uller spaces of Riemann surfaces, we prove a new result showing that a family of Jordan curves varies real-analytically over a simply connected complex Banach manifold and as quasiconformal images of the one at the basepoint, provided that a finite number of marked points on the Jordan curves vary holomorphically over the same parameter space.
item.dc:creator: Xinlong Dong, Arshiya Farhath. G, Sudeb Mitra
